items.q: In the appearance table, 'pale/white' urine is paired with increased water intake while 'light yellow' is labelled normal.
opts: True — those are the first two rows of the table
False — pale/white marks concentration, light yellow marks dilution
True — and both rows are listed under pathological colours
False — light yellow is paired with increased water intake
items.exp: Rows 1 and 2 of the APPEARANCE table: Light yellow → Normal; Pale/white → ↑ water intake (the photo beside the table is captioned 'Normal urine colour'). (Book p740)

items.q: Fill up: Green urine in the appearance table is attributed to triamterene, which the page brackets as a ______ blocker.
items.exp: The row reads 'Green — Triamterene (ENaC blocker)'. (Book p740)

items.q: Orange urine in the table is attributed to rifampicin together with:
items.exp: Orange → Rifampicin, Entacapone (COMT inhibitor). Imipenem + cilastatin is the darkening-on-standing row, nitrofurantoin gives brown, desferrioxamine gives pink. (Book p740)

items.q: A patient on anti-tuberculosis therapy complains that her urine has turned orange but the dipstick is negative for blood. The table's explanation is:
opts: Rifampicin is a listed cause of orange urine
Bilirubinuria, since orange equals obstructive jaundice
Beetroot ingestion, always a false colour
items.exp: Rifampicin (with entacapone) is printed under 'Orange' in the colour table; a dipstick negative for blood excludes haematuria as the source of colour. (Book p740)
